about: Decoy replies for the judge's leniency check: each cites the right code but makes the wrong point, so the judge must not pass it on the named line. Written 13 Nov, before any judge run on them.

decoys.line: Finds the crash on an empty list (items[0] is undefined)
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "On an empty list toggleAll still builds a new list object; returning the list unchanged when it's empty would save an allocation.", "where": "src/reading-list.ts:34"}]

decoys.line: Finds the crash on an empty list (items[0] is undefined)
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "toggleAll reads list.items[0] directly; naming it `first` would make the intent clearer.", "where": "src/reading-list.ts:34"}]

decoys.line: Finds that deciding by the first book breaks AC-1 for a mixed list
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "toggleAll decides from the first book's state, which matches AC-1: a person marks all read from a list that is usually all unread, so the first book is a fair sample.", "where": "src/reading-list.ts:34"}]

decoys.line: Finds that deciding by the first book breaks AC-1 for a mixed list
decoys.reply: [{"id": "d", "severity": "minor", "text": "The first book's read state is computed inside toggleAll on every call; cache it in a variable outside the map for performance.", "where": "src/reading-list.ts:35"}]
